title: Print the generic recommended project workflow
lead: There is no command that prints a recommended workflow for an arbitrary project. `slicer ai instructions` is the agent quick start, and a handoff project changes its step 4. The recommended workflow should be one generic document, the same for every project, stored where a person can edit it, and printed by the tool.
findings_note: user request: a command that prints a generic recommended workflow for any project, kept in docs and updated when the slicer process changes
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing `slicer ai instructions`, the skill, or `implement_finish` (s186); rewriting the implement prompt or getting-started section 6 (s187); slicer's own contributor steps (`tests/affected.py`, the unit suite, or `.worktrees/`).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A person or an agent starting a project needs the same kind of guidelines this repository uses, stated so they fit any project: pick up one slice, start it, do the work, check it, and finish the way the project is configured. That text has to live in the repo, and a process change that should change the guidelines has to update it in the same change. The installed command has to print that text without reading the project.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `docs/generic-recommended-project-workflow.md` (the only edited source of the text)
- `src/slicer/cli.py` (the command)
- `src/slicer/ai.py` or a small reader next to it
- `pyproject.toml`, only if the wheel needs the file listed as package data
- `tests/test_ai.py` or `tests/test_workflow.py`
- `README.md`
- `docs/commands.md`
- `docs/agents.md`
- `docs/getting-started.md` (one pointer, not a rewrite of the loop)
- `CHANGELOG.md`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `test_RecommendedWorkflow_PrintsTheDocsFile`: with no project, `slicer recommended-workflow` exits 0, writes nothing, leaves stderr empty, and its stdout is the exact text of `docs/generic-recommended-project-workflow.md`.
2. `test_RecommendedWorkflow_JsonMatchesTheText`: `--json` exits 0 and returns `{"workflow": "<that same text>"}`. The text and JSON forms carry the same document.
3. `test_RecommendedWorkflow_IgnoresTheProject`: a project with `implement_finish` of `done` and one with `handoff` both print the same stdout as a directory with no project. The command does not lock or write.
4. `test_RecommendedWorkflow_StatesTheGenericGuidelines`: the document contains `slicer sections`, `slicer next --ready`, `slicer start ID --render --strict`, `slicer check`, `implement_finish`, `slicer handoff ID --render`, and `slicer done ID`. It says to follow step 4 of `slicer ai instructions`. It says this file is updated when the recommended workflow changes. It does not name `tests/affected.py`, `.worktrees/`, or `python3 -m unittest discover`.
5. `test_RecommendedWorkflow_MissingFile_IsIo`: when the reader is pointed at a path that is not there, the command exits 3 with code `io` and the message names that path. Nothing is written.
6. `slicer --help` lists `recommended-workflow`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add `slicer recommended-workflow`. It takes the shared flags, including `--json`, and no others. Help text: print the generic recommended project workflow. It does not load a project, lock, or write. It does not warn when no project is present.

The only committed source is `docs/generic-recommended-project-workflow.md`. The command prints that file's text. An editable checkout and an installed wheel both print it. Do not commit a second copy that can drift. A package-data entry or a symlink into the package is enough, as long as the docs file remains the file a person edits.

If the file cannot be read, exit 3 with code `io` and name the path.

Write the document as generic advice for any project, in this order:

- Say that this is the recommended workflow for any project using slicer, that `slicer recommended-workflow` prints this file, and that a change to the recommended workflow updates this file in the same change. `slicer ai instructions` stays the agent quick start and can vary by project; this file does not.
- Read the project's own instructions before acting. Follow its tests and constraints.
- Read and change goals, items, slices, notes, history, and roadmap prose with slicer commands. Do not hand-edit tracking JSON or generated `.slicer/render/` output. When render files conflict, run `slicer render` and then `slicer check`.
- Pick up one slice with `slicer sections` and `slicer next --ready`, using the section names the project configures. Read the scope, dependencies, and checks before starting. Resolve a missing or ambiguous specification first. A row with no slice needs `promote` and a written specification.
- Start with `slicer start ID --render --strict`.
- Do the slice, update the documentation it names, and run the tests the project documents. Then run `slicer check`.
- Finish by following step 4 of `slicer ai instructions`. That is `slicer done ID --note "Describe the verified outcome" --render` unless `implement_finish` is `handoff`, in which case it is `slicer handoff ID --render`. Then run `slicer check`. When step 4 was handoff, run `done` only after review and merge.
- Commit or publish only when the project's instructions or the owner ask. slicer itself never commits, pushes, or tags.
- Work one slice at a time. Isolate it, review it, then integrate it.

In `README.md` and `docs/commands.md`, add the command: it prints `docs/generic-recommended-project-workflow.md`, does not read the project, and supports `--json` as `{"workflow": "..."}`. Say that a change to the recommended workflow updates that file in the same change.

In `docs/agents.md`, add the command to the payload table. In `docs/getting-started.md`, add one sentence next to the existing pointer to `slicer ai instructions`, pointing at `slicer recommended-workflow` for the generic project workflow. Do not rewrite section 6.

CHANGELOG under `[Unreleased]`, `### Added`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, `slicer check`, and `git diff --check`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, including the workflow document, the command, the doc updates, and the changelog entry.
